answer: The prover commits to a set inclusion proof over the registry of claimants, and the proof is small because it carries the exclusion of every competing holder, so two identities claiming the same resource would have to produce contradictory proofs. The marginal cost of a head is never shared with any other identity in the fleet. The ember is the unique resource, the basalt the proof that excludes every other holder, and the forge the registry that makes the exclusion checkable; cloning the ember forces two contradictory basalt proofs, and the forge is where the contradiction shows.
